narrative: Material PL3__M9A920CD exhibits moderate daily demand variability (CV=0.669) with a gamma-distributed profile and no significant trend over the observation period. Lead times are highly unstable (CV=0.793), making transport variability the dominant driver of safety stock requirements. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy is recommended, with order quantity capped at 3,602 units due to the 4,236-unit storage constraint. The policy achieves 95% service level while reducing total annual costs by 95.7% vs. the current SAP baseline.
warnings: Lead time highly variable (CV=0.793) - consider supplier performance improvement
Storage utilization >99.99% after replenishment - minimal physical buffer remains; warehouse capacity review recommended
Unconstrained EOQ (10,602 units) exceeds storage; order quantity hard-capped at 3,602 units

research_insights.selection_rationale: The material has moderate-to-high daily demand with measurable lead-time variance, making a continuous-review (r,Q) policy appropriate. The reorder point covers expected demand during effective lead time plus a safety buffer, and the fixed order quantity minimises total ordering and holding costs subject to the storage capacity constraint.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity binds tightly: safety_stock (634) + order_quantity (3,602) = 4,236 units, just below the 4,236.495-unit limit. Any upward rounding or unplanned over-delivery could breach capacity. Recommend a formal capacity review to either increase storage by ~200 units or accept a slightly smaller order quantity (3,500 units) with marginally higher ordering frequency.
